questions.prompt: What does a TypeScript type assertion do?
options: It changes the JavaScript value into a different object.
It guarantees the asserted type is correct.
It tells the compiler to treat an expression as a type; it does not validate the value at runtime.
It inserts a runtime validator for every field.
questions.answer_key: It tells the compiler to treat an expression as a type; it does not validate the value at runtime.
questions.explanation: Use an assertion only when independent evidence justifies it; validation is separate.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Type Assertions”?
options: The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with assertion syntax and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with assertion syntax and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Assertion syntax”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Type Assertions”?
options: Check when assertions are justified, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume risks of incorrectly asserting a type is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
questions.answer_key: Check when assertions are justified, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “When assertions are justified”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
